summary: Grant CS/Sales read-only access to Dedicated Burst beta Grafana dashboards + interpretation guide
description:
Request from CS + Sales enablement: we need read-only access to the Dedicated Burst beta dashboards so we can (a) onboard beta customers, (b) answer real-time questions about denials/limits, and (c) support escalations without pulling SRE into every call.

Scope
- Grant access for a limited set of CS/Sales users to the Grafana folder(s) used for burst beta.
- Provide a short, practical guide on how to interpret the key panels (what “good” looks like vs when to escalate).
- Ensure we do not expose cross-tenant sensitive data (no browsing other customers by default; tenant dashboards should be filtered/templated).

Requested users / groups
- CS: Rachel Kim, Miguel Santos, Markus Klein, Simran Kaur
- Sales enablement: Stephanie Nguyen, Lukas Meyer

Target dashboards (names as shown in Grafana)
1) Dedicated Burst — Overview (per tenant)
2) Burst Pools — Regional Saturation
3) Burst Denials — Reasons & Rate
4) Neighbor Impact — Non-burst SLO Guardrails

Acceptance criteria
- Above users can open dashboards via SSO, view-only.
- Default dashboard variables land on “tenant = <select>” without showing an unfiltered multi-tenant view.
- Add a brief interpretation section (below) to the ticket and link it from the CS onboarding checklist.

Security/permissions notes
- Read-only access only.
- Prefer access via Okta group -> Grafana Team mapping.
- If any dashboard contains multi-tenant data, it must be restricted to SRE/Eng only, or variables must be constrained to a tenant allow-list.

Due date driver
- Beta onboarding calls are scheduled next week; we need this before the next onboarding sync.

interpretation_guide:
Dashboard interpretation guide (CS/Sales)

1) Dedicated Burst — Overview (per tenant)
- “Baseline vs Burst Usage”: Baseline = reserved capacity; Burst = borrowed from managed burst pools. If Burst is flat at 0 during a customer-reported peak, check Denials by reason.
- “Burst Utilization % of Tenant Cap”: If near 100% and denials occur, the customer is hitting their configured cap (expected). Action: recommend increasing cap/temporary override via internal process (link INT-9132) if approved.
- “Admission Decision Latency”: If admission latency spikes, customer may see timeouts/retries. Escalate if sustained >2–3 minutes or correlated with 5xx.

2) Burst Pools — Regional Saturation
- “Pool Saturation %”: If >85–90% sustained, denials will increase for lower priority tiers. This is a fleet capacity signal. Action: explain expected behavior; escalate to Fleet/SRE if pool saturation persists and impacts multiple tenants.
- “Queue Depth / Backpressure”: Rising queue depth with stable traffic suggests capacity constraint or telemetry issues. If queue grows rapidly, check circuit breaker panel.

3) Burst Denials — Reasons & Rate
Common denial reasons (customer-friendly phrasing):
- TENANT_CAP_REACHED: Customer’s burst cap reached (config limit). Expected; they can retry after cooldown or increase cap.
- POOL_SATURATED: Burst pool has insufficient headroom. Expected during regional peaks; recommend smoothing load or scheduling; escalate if prolonged.
- COOLDOWN_ACTIVE: Customer recently burst and is in cooldown window. Expected; advise backoff.
- FLEET_SAFETY_GUARD: Global safety cap or SLO gate triggered to protect non-burst tenants. This is a “platform protection” event. Escalate to SRE if frequent.
- POLICY_CONFIG_INVALID: Tenant config issue or mismatch. Escalate to Platform.

4) Neighbor Impact — Non-burst SLO Guardrails
- “Non-burst p95 latency delta”: This is the primary neighbor impact indicator. If delta breaches the annotated threshold for >5–10 minutes, the SLO gate may reduce/disable burst automatically. Escalate to SRE if sustained.
- “Tail amplification”: If tail grows while average is stable, suspect noisy-neighbor symptoms; confirm whether circuit breaker is active.

Telemetry lag panel
- “Telemetry lag (seconds)”: Measures freshness of capacity signals used by admission control/routing. If lag spikes, admission decisions may become more conservative (more denials) to preserve determinism and safety.
- Rule of thumb: brief spikes (<60s) are usually benign; sustained lag (>2–3 minutes) during customer impact should be escalated.

When to escalate immediately (CS/Sales)
- Admission timeouts/errors spike (customer sees 5xx/timeout correlated with burst).
- Circuit breaker is ON for the customer’s region/hardware class.
- Non-burst p95 latency delta breaches guardrail threshold.

Links
- Overload mitigation runbook: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/burst-pool-overload-mitigation-runbook.json
- SLOs/alerting context: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/dedicated-burst-slos-and-alerting.json
resolution: Access granted via Okta->Grafana team mapping with Viewer role. CS/Sales-safe versions of burst dashboards placed in dedicated folders; multi-tenant debugging panel removed. Added a practical interpretation guide and linked to SRE runbook/SLO doc for escalation criteria.
